assessment.nobel_worthiness: Turned a biological process, regulated protein degradation, into a designable chemical reaction: bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues recruit E3 ligases to chosen targets. Originality is high, the concept is general, and clinical degraders now validate it. A strong fit for chemistry of life with direct biomedical consequence.
assessment.attribution: Crews (PROTAC concept and first degraders, later clinical translation), Deshaies (early PROTAC work, cullin-RING ligase biochemistry) and Handa (cereblon as thalidomide target) are the clearest trio from the credited names. Ciulli and Gray are major contributors, so the cut is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Independent reproduction is extensive across many labs and targets, and clinical trial data exist. Mechanism, including ternary complex formation, is well defined. Timing looks reasonable, though approved degrader drugs are still few.
uncertainties: Whether recognition should split PROTACs from molecular glues or from thalidomide-cereblon biology.
Allocation between Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli and Gray is unresolved.
Clinical benefit is not yet fully established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing by synthesis changed the measurement of nucleic acids by many orders of magnitude and underlies genome, mutation and cancer research. It is a chemistry-driven analytical invention: reversible terminator chemistry and single-molecule detection.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived and developed the Solexa chemistry; Rothberg (pyrosequencing-based platform) and Mayer (parallel sequencing concepts) also contributed. Which of the two platform lineages deserves recognition is a real allocation question.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with decades of independent use and universal adoption; recognition is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Competing technology lineages (pyrosequencing versus reversible terminators) complicate credit.
I am relying on memory of the Solexa history rather than verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reversible m6A methylation showed that RNA carries a dynamic chemical regulatory layer, with writers, erasers and readers. It gave a clear chemical basis for a biological regulatory process and opened epitranscriptomics.
assessment.attribution: He proposed reversible RNA methylation and identified FTO as an m6A demethylase; Jaffrey and Rechavi (with Dominissini) provided transcriptome-wide m6A mapping. Writer and reader discoveries by other credited people complicate a three-person split.
assessment.maturity: Core findings are broadly reproduced, but physiological interpretation, mapping artefacts and quantitative stoichiometry are still debated. Reasonably mature but not fully settled.
uncertainties: Disputes over FTO substrate specificity and mapping accuracy.
Many contributors to writer, reader and eraser discoveries; fair allocation is unclear.
Possible overlap with a Medicine-type recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one DNA base to another without double-strand breaks, using deaminase chemistry on a programmable scaffold. They are a general tool with strong therapeutic relevance and clear originality.
assessment.attribution: Liu conceived and led the work and is the decisive contributor; Komor and Gaudelli were lead researchers in his lab. Nishida and Kondo made a parallel cytidine deaminase editor, which could be argued as a competing credit.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups reproduce base editing and clinical trials are underway. Timing is somewhat early for a full verdict on lasting impact.
uncertainties: Overlap with CRISPR recognition from 2020 and with prime editing (B056).
Long-term safety, off-target effects and clinical outcomes are not yet settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mass spectrometry proteomics, with shotgun, quantitative and targeted approaches, made large-scale measurement of protein abundance, modification and interactions routine. It is a measurement foundation for biochemistry and medicine, and I value rigorous quantification.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Aebersold and Yates cover the main methodological pillars (high-resolution MS-based proteomics, quantitative and targeted proteomics, shotgun/MudPIT), but Hunt, Gygi and Heck also made decisive contributions, so any three-way split leaves out important people.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and independently validated over decades. Recognition is timely, and it partly overlaps with the 2002 ionization recognition.
uncertainties: Several equally credible contributors; the three-name cut is difficult to defend.
Overlap with earlier MS prizes could be held against it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat showed that mutant KRAS cysteine can be targeted covalently, which broke a long-standing 'undruggable' barrier, and his chemical genetics of analog-sensitive kinases gave biologists a general tool. Sotorasib and related drugs followed.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is clean for the covalent KRAS G12C strategy and chemical genetics, with Shokat as sole credited name. The drug development was carried out by many companies, but the foundational chemistry is his.
assessment.maturity: KRAS G12C inhibitors are approved and independently reproduced, but durability of clinical response and resistance remain active issues. Timely, perhaps slightly early.
uncertainties: Clinical resistance limits the long-term picture.
A sole laureate is unusual, and the chemical genetics and KRAS achievements could be questioned as two discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing converts single-molecule chemistry into an electrical signal and now sequences DNA and RNA directly, including modifications. It is original, practical and still expanding.
assessment.attribution: Deamer and Branton conceived reading polynucleotides through a pore, Kasianowicz demonstrated translocation, Bayley engineered protein pores, and Akeson showed enzyme-controlled ratcheting. Credit is spread, and the proposed trio omits Branton and Kasianowicz.
assessment.maturity: Commercial devices are widely used and independently validated, though accuracy for some applications is still improving. Maturity is good.
uncertainties: I am unsure of the current status of some credited people, which matters for eligibility.
Allocation among five people is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Activity-based protein profiling uses reactive probes to measure enzyme activity directly rather than abundance, in native proteomes. It is a general chemical tool, linking enzymology to biology and drug discovery, including covalent ligand screening.
assessment.attribution: Cravatt is the central figure for the proteome-wide extension and its use in discovery; Bogyo, Overkleeft and Weerapana made important contributions. A single-laureate configuration is defensible, but credit is shared.
assessment.maturity: The method is widely adopted and independently reproduced, and covalent chemoproteomics is currently productive. It is somewhat younger than other candidates and impact on medicines is still maturing.
uncertainties: Whether the contribution is broad enough compared with other chemical biology candidates.
Credit sharing with Bogyo, Overkleeft and others.
